topic: Why setting micro goals tricks your brain into starting hard tasks

script.title: Micro Goals Trick Your Brain into Starting Hard Tasks
script.hook: Why does opening a document instantly cure your procrastination?

scenes.text: Why does opening a document instantly cure your procrastination?
Your brain views massive tasks as physical threats.
When you attempt to write an entire report, your amygdala panics.
So it triggers friction, forcing you to check your phone instead.

motion_action.query_text: why do I procrastinate on big tasks
motion_action.result_headline: Task size triggers perceived cognitive threat

scenes.text: To bypass this alarm system, you must make the goal absurdly small.
Tell yourself you will only write for two minutes.
Suddenly, the friction drops to near zero.
Once you take action, psychological momentum takes over.
Psychologists call this the Zeigarnik effect.

motion_action.title: COGNITIVE PRINCIPLE
motion_action.highlight_text: ZEIGARNIK EFFECT: INCOMPLETE TASKS OCCUPY THOUGHT

scenes.text: Your brain hates unfinished business and pushes you to keep going.

script.description:
Learn how setting micro goals tricks your brain to overcome procrastination instantly. Discover the psychological science behind the Zeigarnik effect and task completion. Small habits reduce mental friction so you can focus faster.
